notes: Alert conditions over the typed analytics event stream (see docs/OBSERVABILITY.md). Every `event` value must be a member of ANALYTICS_EVENT_NAMES in @pickle/analytics — enforced by packages/analytics/test/observability.test.ts. Thresholds are initial operating points to be tuned against real traffic; they are versioned here so tuning is a reviewed change, never a dashboard edit.

alerts.name: Crash spike
alerts.runbook: Group by appBuild + platform; a spike isolated to one build means halt rollout of that build.

alerts.name: Analysis failure spike
alerts.runbook: Group by failureKind and modelVersion; correlate with capture_envelope_verdict overall=UNSUPPORTED share to separate capture-quality drift from pipeline regressions.

alerts.name: Abstention spike on supported captures
alerts.runbook: Break down by reasonCategory. Excess abstention on SUPPORTED-envelope captures is a P1 (silent product failure); join against capture_envelope_verdict by sessionId.

alerts.name: Analysis latency spike
alerts.runbook: Compare p95 by modelVersion and deviceClass against the previous 24h; a regression isolated to one model version means roll that version back.

alerts.name: Target lock failure spike
alerts.runbook: Group by reason (no_lock vs ambiguity_timeout) and algorithmVersion; a spike after an acquisition change is a rollback signal (D-027 gate).

alerts.name: Event proposal failure spike
alerts.runbook: Correlate with capture_envelope_verdict; failures on SUPPORTED captures indicate an event-proposal regression, not capture quality.

alerts.name: API backend error spike
alerts.runbook: Group by route + errorCode; check DB/queue health first (catalog.db_unavailable dominates when Postgres is down).

alerts.name: Auth failure spike (security-sensitive)
alerts.runbook: Sudden 401/403 volume means either a broken client build or credential stuffing; check distribution across routes — a single-route concentration on auth endpoints is an attack signal. Escalate to security review, never silence.

alerts.name: Worker failure spike
alerts.runbook: handler_exception means a poison job or code bug (check worker logs by timestamp); sustained 'unhandled' means a capability (ffmpeg, object store) is unconfigured in the deployment.

alerts.name: Queue backlog growth
alerts.runbook: Depth persistently above threshold means consumers are down or too slow; deletion/purge jobs backing up is ALSO a privacy-SLA risk (directive §58) — treat sustained backlog as security-adjacent.

alerts.name: Training-consent change anomaly (security-sensitive)
alerts.runbook: A grant-rate step change without a matching product release suggests a consent-UI defect enrolling users unintentionally — freeze training-data intake until verified.

alerts.name: Account deletion request spike
alerts.runbook: Deletion spikes follow trust incidents; verify the §58 deletion pipeline is draining (queue_backlog + worker_failure) so requests complete within SLA.
